The '''Zorbia system''' was among the [[Outer Moddell systems]] in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]], one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]] within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]]. The [[Star system/Legends|system]] was located on the edge of the [[Monsua Nebula/Legends|Monsua Nebula]] and lay on the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Ovise Reach/Legends|Ovise Reach]], connecting it to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor]] and [[Trindello system]]s.<ref name="TEA" /> The Zorbia system contained three [[Planet/Legends|planets]], including [[Zorbia II]] at its second [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position. Zorbia II's [[Local day/Legends|local days]] lasted twenty-eight [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], and the planet had a 360-day-long [[local year]].<ref name="Gamer" />

Zorbia II was [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to thirty million [[Human/Legends|Humans]] who were known as the [[Zorbian space pirates]]. The [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] were thought to have [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] roots and had been a nuisance in the surrounding Outer Moddell systems for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]]; they were known to attack both each other and traveling [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="Gamer" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Zorbia system was first mentioned in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was authored by [[Craig Robert Carey]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Jason Fry]] and published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Gamer" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the system in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />
